messages:
anika: spinning up marble11b int4 canary today. seeing rare OOMs on long multi-turn QA when prefetch is on. tagging infra + eng-ml.

ron: thanks — dedicated canary pool or hosted? what GPU family?

anika: dedicated pool (A100/P4d mix). frequency ~1/12 requests. stack points to big KV prefetch allocations during long prompt contexts.

lucas: what's current config? batch, max_new_tokens, prefetch heuristic?

anika: defaults used by rollout: batch_size=2, max_new_tokens=200, prefetch=true, prefetch.heuristic=bulk_load

taylor: bulk_load + high max_new_tokens is a red flag. two approaches that worked elsewhere: 1) make max_new_tokens dynamic by prompt length (cap at 128), e.g. dynamic_max_new = min(128, max(32, prompt_len * 2)); 2) enable soft-reserve on allocator freelist to avoid large immediate cudaMallocs: `allocator.soft_reserve_ratio=0.15`.

lucas: also consider `allocator.defrag.pre_batch=true` to run a quick micro-defrag right before batches that will trigger prefetch. cheaper than full compaction.

anika: ok rolling quick change for canary: set max_new_tokens dynamic per prompt, allocator.soft_reserve_ratio=0.15, defrag.pre_batch=true. leaving prefetch heuristic as kv_scan (so we avoid aggressive bulk loads). command: 
```
redwoodctl config set marble11b --default.max_new_tokens=dynamic_max_by_prompt --allocator.soft_reserve_ratio=0.15 --allocator.defrag_pre_batch=true --prefetch.heuristic=kv_scan
```

dev-bot: [alert] canary marble11b v0.4.0 failure-rate=2.9% at 6601234575. rollout controller paused.

anika: saw the pause. after pause I dug allocator stats at spike: 
```
heap_total: 24GB
available_gpu_mem: 22.8GB
freelist_count: 6
soft_reserved: 3.6GB
fragmentation_ratio: 0.79
compaction_runs_last_5min: 0
avg_alloc_ms: 2.3
```

ron: frag 0.79 close to 0.8 threshold; compactor didn't run. soft_reserve helps but frag still near threshold. Two safe next steps: lower compactor threshold for the pool to 0.72 and add `prefetch.streaming=true` fallback so if prefetch would add >X MB it streams tokens instead of preallocating.

lucas: also instrument a heuristic: if predicted prefetch footprint > 1.5GB then convert request to streaming mode. we can compute predicted footprint from prompt token counts and cached KV sizes.

anika: implemented pool change and streaming fallback: 
```
redwoodctl feature set --pool canary-marble --allocator.frag_threshold=0.72
redwoodctl config set marble11b --prefetch.streaming_threshold_mb=1536
```

anika: after change ran 15k requests: OOMs dropped to 0, p95 latency increased ~22ms for the canary due to some streaming fallbacks. throughput steady.

ron: can we add an automated rollout rule to reduce blast radius? e.g. if failure_rate>1% OR compaction_runs_last_5min==0 AND fragmentation>0.75 FOR 5m -> disable prefetch for model/pool.

taylor: propose policy DSL: 
```
policy {
  trigger: failure_rate > 0.01 OR (fragmentation_ratio > 0.75 AND compaction_runs_last_5min == 0) FOR 5m
  action: set model.config.prefetch=false
}
```

anika: added that policy to canary. also queued an eval to confirm dynamic max_new doesn't harm QA. initial quick-run EM diff: -0.08% (within noise). full eval scheduled. eval-id=eval-6601234590.

lucas: great. for onboarding defaults for marble11b suggest: batch_size=1-2 (auto adjust), default_max_new=dynamic_by_prompt (cap=128), allocator.soft_reserve_ratio=0.15, frag_threshold=0.72, defrag_pre_batch=true, prefetch.streaming_threshold_mb=1536. include rollout guard policy we just added.

anika: drafting onboarding doc with those defaults + a checklist: run 50k requests sim with QA prompts, capture heap-stats traces, ensure compaction runs at expected thresholds, run nightly EM/F1 eval.

taylor: add a stress test that simulates spikes by concatenating multi-turn dialogues to ensure streaming fallback triggers.

anika: will add to the onboarding harness. thanks all :rocket:

dev-bot: [info] eval queued: eval-6601234590
